major_event: MyConstant paused deposits and withdrawals on 17 November 2022, announced an intended orderly liquidation on 25 November 2022, and was ordered by California DFPI to cease offering its peer-to-peer lending and interest-bearing products

duplicate_check.notes: No MyConstant, CONST LLC, My Constant, or matching myconstant.com platform record was found in canonical data or consumed candidate history.

notes: MyConstant is a historically significant mixed CeFi lending and interest-account platform. California DFPI records state that the operator offered crypto-collateralized peer-to-peer loan brokering, a fixed-yield crypto account, and a fixed-return fiat account; paused consumer deposits and withdrawals on 17 November 2022; and told customers on 25 November 2022 that it intended to implement an orderly liquidation. The later DFPI order found California-law violations and required the relevant products to cease in California. Canonical promotion must separate the three product families, distinguish the operator's liquidation statement from the regulator's legal findings, identify any later liquidation or recovery process, and avoid inferring bankruptcy, fraud, repayment completion, recovery rate, collateral sufficiency, or a final end date without reviewed evidence.

major_event: Abra began winding down Abra Earn for United States customers in June 2023, later entered a multistate asset-return settlement, and resolved SEC charges concerning the unregistered interest-account product

duplicate_check.notes: No Abra Earn, Plutus Lending LLC, Abra Interest Account, or matching product-scoped Abra lending record was found in canonical data or consumed candidate history.

notes: Promote only as a product-scoped historical crypto interest-account record, separate from Abra's wallet, trading, institutional, and later corporate activity. The SEC states that Abra Earn launched in the United States around July 2020, reached approximately $600 million in assets, and began winding down in June 2023 with United States customers instructed to withdraw. The CSBS multistate settlement covers remaining virtual assets for United States Abra Trade customers in participating states and describes up to $82.1 million to be returned; that settlement population must not be silently treated as identical to every Abra Earn customer or as proof that all withdrawals completed. Canonical review must preserve the Plutus Lending legal-entity boundary, distinguish Earn balances from Trade accounts, separate the 2024 settlement from the SEC case and 2025 final judgment, and avoid inferring customer harm, universal repayment completion, or a recovery percentage beyond the reviewed orders.
